patients.summary: Self-employed handyman who joined in 2019 with treated hypertension and an old duodenal ulcer. An unrecognized anterior MI surfaces in late 2022 as HFrEF with an LV aneurysm, followed by LAD stenting, Dressler syndrome, a neck injury with neuropathic hand pain, two heart-failure admissions and an NSAID-related duodenal ulcer bleed in 2026.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Babcock called about membership. Says his old doctor's office keeps rolling him to a different covering provider every time and he can never get through on the phone. Works for himself as a handyman, wants evening or early-morning slots when possible. Membership agreement and welcome packet emailed. Records release signed electronically and sent to his prior primary care office. New patient visit set for 9/10 at 8:00.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M here to establish. Self-employed handyman (carpentry, small repairs, some roofing), lives alone in Granby, divorced. Previous PCP office he describes as hard to reach.

PMH
- HTN, on lisinopril 20 for about 8 years. Home cuff log he brought is at goal.
- Duodenal ulcer 2015: had black stools, scoped at his old practice, ulcer in the duodenum, H. pylori positive, treated, did a course of acid blocker afterward and stopped it. Nothing since.
- Neck: stiff for years, worse turning to back out of a driveway. Was told the neck films showed arthritis/disc wear. No arm symptoms.
No surgeries. NKDA.

Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, aspirin 81 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily. Aspirin and statin were started by the old PCP for prevention given BP, smoking history and his father's heart attack. He has no cholesterol diagnosis he knows of.

FH: father MI at 58. Mother arthritis. Brother has high blood pressure.
SH: smoked about a pack a day for 20 years, quit 2014. 1-2 drinks a month. No drugs.

ROS: no chest pain, no exertional breathlessness, no leg swelling, no melena since 2015, no reflux symptoms.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck: rotation mildly limited both ways, no tenderness. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro: strength and reflexes symmetric in the arms.

A/P
1. Hypertension, at goal on lisinopril 20. Continue.
2. Prevention: aspirin and atorvastatin continue for now; lipids today.
3. History of duodenal ulcer, quiet for 4 years. If he ever needs an anti-inflammatory he is to call first.
4. Cervical spondylosis, mechanical, stable.
5. Health maintenance: Tdap today. CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH, one-time HCV and HIV screens. He qualifies for lung screening (20 pk-yr, quit 5 yr ago) and wants it: LDCT ordered. Colonoscopy 2017 per his report, getting the record. Flu shot when the vaccine arrives next month.
RTC 5-6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Alan, your labs from Tuesday look good. Blood counts, kidney function, liver tests and thyroid are normal. A1c is 5.6, which is in the normal range. Cholesterol numbers are where we want them on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 46 pages, scanned to media. Summary for the chart:
- 2015: evaluated for dark stools; upper endoscopy at an outside GI group showed a duodenal ulcer; biopsy positive for H. pylori; treated with a 14-day eradication regimen, then 8 weeks of a proton pump inhibitor. Stool antigen after treatment negative. PPI stopped.
- 2016: cervical spine x-rays for neck stiffness: multilevel disc space narrowing and facet degenerative change, no fracture or listhesis.
- 2017: screening colonoscopy, complete exam, no polyps or other findings; 10-year interval recommended.
- Hypertension managed on lisinopril 20 mg; aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg on the list.
- Allergies: none recorded.
Abstracted by MA; PCP reviewed.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative. VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, on his way to a job in Southwick.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Mediastinum: no lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: LDCT negative, Lung-RADS 1. Repeat next November. Patient notified via portal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP check. Home readings fine, mostly under 130 systolic. No lightheadedness. Busy with indoor jobs this winter. Neck about the same. No GI symptoms.
Exam: BP at goal today. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: HTN controlled, continue lisinopril 20. BMP for K/Cr. He turns 65 in May; reviewed Medicare enrollment timing, he is signing up for Part B starting June. Welcome to Medicare visit this summer.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for lisinopril 20 mg. Patient asked for 90-day supply so he does not have to go in during the shutdown. Sent 90 days x 1 refill per protocol.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Welcome to Medicare visit, masks on. Feels well. Working steadily, mostly outdoor jobs now. No chest pain or breathlessness carrying lumber or on ladders. No black stools.
Functional: independent, drives, manages own meds and money. Hearing fine by whisper test. No falls. Home safety reviewed; he is careful on roofs and uses a harness.
Depression screen negative. Alcohol low.
Exam: vitals as charted. Visual acuity by chart normal with readers. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd no pulsatile mass. Ext no edema.
Plan: CBC, CMP, lipids. Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. AAA ultrasound once (ever-smoker). LDCT due November. Colonoscopy 2017 normal, next 2027. Advance directive packet given; he wants his brother as his health care agent and will bring the form back.

reports.text: Limited ultrasound of the abdominal aorta for aneurysm screening. The aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation and is normal in caliber throughout, maximal diameter 2.1 cm. No aneurysm. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.

documents.title: AAA screen
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aorta normal caliber, no aneurysm. One-time screen complete, no repeat needed.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu high-dose L deltoid, Shingrix dose 2 R deltoid. He remembers the first Shingrix made his arm ache for two days; advised acetaminophen if needed, not ibuprofen given his ulcer history. Observed 15 min, fine. Shingles series complete.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Technique: low-dose noncontrast CT chest. Comparison: 11/2019. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Annual LDCT negative again, Lung-RADS 1. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his truck after a job, parked. Identity verified. Home BP log for the last month is at goal. Taking lisinopril, aspirin, atorvastatin daily. No side effects. Neck stiff in the cold, nothing radiating. Asked about the COVID vaccine: eligible at 65, helped him find a pharmacy appointment.
A/P: HTN controlled. BMP at the lab this week. Next in-person visit at the summer wellness visit.

documents.title: BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium normal. No changes.

documents.title: Outside immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State registry shows Pfizer COVID dose 1 given 3/5/21 at a retail pharmacy. Added to immunization history.

documents.title: Second shot done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the 2nd covid shot yesterday. Felt like I got hit by a truck last night, chills, but better this morning. Just letting you know for my record.

documents.title: RE: Second shot done
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks Alan, that reaction is common after dose two and should be gone in a day or so. Fluids and rest, acetaminophen if needed. We've added the dose to your record.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Doing well. Busy summer, deck rebuilds. Exercise is his work. No chest discomfort, no breathlessness on ladders, no ankle swelling. Occasional neck stiffness in the morning, unchanged.
Screens: PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C low. No falls. Lives alone, brother nearby. Health care proxy form returned, brother named, scanned.
Exam: vitals as charted, BP at goal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: CMP, lipids, CBC. Flu in the fall; pneumococcal vaccine this fall too. LDCT November. Continue current meds.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fluzone high-dose L deltoid. No issues. Pneumococcal not yet stocked, will call him when the new 20-valent arrives.

documents.title: Immunization

documents.body: PCV20 given IM R deltoid. No prior pneumococcal vaccines per records. Single dose completes the series.

reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Return to annual screening.
